findings.summary: Frontmatter-validator-coverage subsection contradicts v4's own surgical corrections in four ways; would mechanically reject the agents v4 declares correct
findings.location: blueprint-v4.md §Agent Frontmatter Specifications → Frontmatter validator coverage (lines 1081-1091)
findings.description: The 'Frontmatter validator coverage' subsection prescribes what the FR-6 validator (`validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py`) should enforce on agent frontmatter. As written in v4, the subsection is internally inconsistent with v4's own corrections in the YAML blocks immediately above it and the convention notes at lines 962-975. Four specific contradictions: (1) Line 1085 lists `memory` among 'five required fields' that the validator must verify present; but v4 explicitly omits `memory` from three of the five new agents (execute-task-code-producer, execute-task-quality-handler, execute-phase-quality-reviewer) per the v4 surgical correction documented in the frontmatter `re_author_reason` field. The validator-as-spec'd would FAIL those three agents that v4 declares correct. (2) Line 1086 says `Task` is 'a synonym for TaskCreate', whereas convention note 2 (lines 966-970) explicitly states they are TWO SEPARATE TOOL FAMILIES — Agent (formerly Task) for subagent dispatch vs TaskCreate/TaskUpdate for task-board management — and that conflating them was the v3-era misreading v4 corrects. The validator-as-spec'd would re-introduce the v3 conflation. (3) Lines 1086 and 1088 treat Gate 4 platform-validity verification as 'pending' ('added to the whitelist after Gate 4 validates them', '`none` pending Gate 4 validation') — but the frontmatter's `re_author_reason` and convention note 3 both state that Gate 4 verification is COMPLETE and that `memory: none` is INVALID. The validator-as-spec'd would still accept the invalid value v4 was authored to remove. (4) Line 1089 declares `effort: ∈ {low, medium, high, xhigh}` but KB-cc-platform/references/extensions.md (the canonical platform docs the v4 corrections cite) explicitly documents `max` as a valid effort value ('max (maximum effort)' — extensions.md line ~181). Validator-as-spec'd would reject agents that legitimately use `effort: max`.

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Lists memory as required-present; calls Task a synonym for TaskCreate; treats `none` as pending Gate 4 validation; omits `max` from effort enum.

v4 surgically fixes both: removes 'memory: none' from 3 agents (omits the field)... changes execute-orchestrator and execute-finalize-reconciler tool lists to use 'Agent' (canonical) for subagent dispatch while preserving 'TaskUpdate'...

There are TWO separate Claude Code tool families that earlier Blueprint versions conflated: Agent (formerly Task pre-v2.1.63) — spawns subagents; TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList — built-in session task-board management. The v3 Blueprint substitution of TaskCreate/TaskUpdate for cc-design's Task was a misreading.

Gate 4 platform-validity verification — UPDATED in v4 with authoritative answers (verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents): (a) memory: none is INVALID — documented valid values are user|project|local; (b) Edit is VALID; (c) non-KB skill binding is VALID.

Documented values are low (minimal thinking, fastest), medium (moderate), high (deep reasoning), xhigh (extended; Opus 4.7 only, falls back to high on other models), max (maximum effort). Source: Claude Code Agent SDK EffortLevel literal.

findings.impact: BLOCKER because this subsection drives Plan-stage task generation for the validator script (validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py). If the validator is implemented as this subsection prescribes, it will reject all three v4-corrected agents that omit memory, perpetuate the v3 Task/TaskCreate conflation in the whitelist, and reject any `effort: max` agent. Per AC-FR-9-c the validator's frontmatter check is the mechanical gate for the FR-9 skill-binding requirement — a misconfigured validator silently degrades the entire FR-6 + FR-9 enforcement story, and any agent definition v4 currently declares correct would be flagged invalid by its own validator spec.
findings.recommended_resolution: Rewrite the Frontmatter validator coverage subsection to reflect v4's resolved state: (a) `memory` is OPTIONAL (omitted = no persistent memory; enum when present = user|project|local; `none` is INVALID and must be REJECTED); (b) `tools:` whitelist must list `Agent` and `TaskUpdate` as separate entries with separate semantics (subagent-dispatch vs task-board-management) and explicitly NOT treat them as synonyms; (c) `Edit` and `Bash(python3:*)` are VALID per Gate 4; (d) `effort:` enum must include `max`. Cross-reference convention notes 1-3 inline so the validator-coverage spec stays tied to the resolved state. Re-author by design-composer in reconciliation cycle 3.

findings.summary: execute-task-quality-handler Bash restriction `Bash(python3:*)` precludes running the non-Python test stacks the 4-phase verification requires
findings.location: blueprint-v4.md §Agent Frontmatter Specifications → execute-task-quality-handler YAML (lines 1020-1029) + rationale (lines 1031-1037)
findings.description: The quality-handler's tools are declared `[Read, Glob, Grep, Bash(python3:*)]`. Per FR-2 + D-11 + Component 3 spec, the quality-handler runs the `ai-development-guide` 4-phase verification (lint → build → test → final gate) on filesModified. Many production test stacks are non-Python: npm/yarn/pnpm test, cargo test, go test, dotnet test, mvn test, etc. The 4-phase pattern explicitly spans the language stack of the modified files; the task spec declares which stack. The Bash restriction silently breaks the quality-handler for any modified-file set whose tests are not python invokable. The v4 rationale acknowledges this: 'Validation needed at runtime — if direct test execution by quality-handler is required, Bash restriction needs to be widened.' Shipping with an acknowledged-but-unfixed contract gap is precisely the silent-absorption failure mode ADR-0029 + ADR-0033 forbid. cc-design.md line 327 (the source-of-truth for this agent's tools) uses unrestricted `[Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]`; the v4 narrowing diverges from the per-layer-design spec without arbitration evidence (no Q-CC-N covers this; no decision in D-2/D-11 mandates the narrowing).

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]. Read for inputs; Bash for invoking detect_stubs.py + lint + test commands.
tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash(python3:*)]

Bash(python3:*) restricted because quality-handler's Bash usage is script-only (detect_stubs.py + acceptance-test runners via python wrappers). If acceptance-tests are non-python (e.g., npm test), the orchestrator runs them and passes results to quality-handler. Validation needed at runtime — if direct test execution by quality-handler is required, Bash restriction needs to be widened.
Runs the ai-development-guide 4-phase verification + detect_stubs.py (Q-CC-2 path-aware patterns).

findings.impact: Operational: any task with non-Python tests will exit the per-task quality loop with infrastructure errors rather than verdict. The handler will return BLOCKER/escalation_needed for routine non-Python tests, triggering false-positive escalations. This compounds Risk 4 (skill-install sequencing) — even with correct binding, the agent can't actually run the tests it's bound to verify. Reduces FR-9 binding to ornamental.
findings.recommended_resolution: Two paths: (a) WIDEN to unrestricted `Bash` matching cc-design.md (the simplest correction; this is what cc-design specifies and the rationale's 'orchestrator runs them' workaround is not in any FR/AC); or (b) RE-ARCHITECT so all test invocation goes through `run_phase_checks.py` (already python-invoked) and quality-handler genuinely only consumes results — but this is a redesign of FR-2's per-task quality loop that needs to be reconciled with D-2c's APPROVED-status return contract and the per-task-execution-result schema. Recommended Path (a) for v5 (minimal change matches per-layer source); flag Path (b) as a candidate follow-on feature if `Bash(python3:*)` is preferred for security narrowing.

findings.summary: New 'auditing-shared as a Skill binding' convention introduced across 4 agents without an ADR; convention note 1 declares the divergence but no ADR ratifies it
findings.location: blueprint-v4.md §Agent Frontmatter Specifications → convention note 1 (line 964); 4 agents binding `auditing-shared` in `skills:` (orchestrator, quality-handler, phase-quality-reviewer, finalize-reconciler)
findings.description: Convention note 1 reads: 'This feature establishes a new convention. The execute-orchestrator, execute-task-quality-handler, execute-phase-quality-reviewer, and execute-finalize-reconciler bind auditing-shared in their skills: field. Existing planning-side agents do not — they invoke auditing-shared scripts via Bash only and never load its SKILL.md as context. The new convention loads the SKILL.md as context (so the agent has the conceptual model of the shared utilities) AND retains Bash invocation for script execution.' The note correctly surfaces the deviation per ADR-0029, but the deviation is a project-wide convention change affecting how all future agents bind auditing-shared. Per the established pattern (ADR-0011 for KB structure conventions, ADR-0019 for naming conventions, ADR-0031 for canonical-helper-home), cross-feature shared-conventions changes warrant an ADR by design-composer. The Blueprint authors ADR-0032 (per-doc-type vocabulary + frontmatter fields), ADR-0033 (Scope-Deviation surfacing extension), ADR-0034 (PRD mis-credit cleanup) but none cover the auditing-shared binding convention. ADR-0032's scope (per its Change 1-5 enumeration and per its own line: 'covers separate housekeeping per its Change 1-5 scope') does NOT include skill-binding conventions. The convention exists in the Blueprint and would be enforced by FR-6 (validator's skills: existence check) without a ratifying ADR.

evidence.quote_paraphrase: This feature establishes a new convention. The execute-orchestrator, execute-task-quality-handler, execute-phase-quality-reviewer, and execute-finalize-reconciler bind auditing-shared in their skills: field. Existing planning-side agents do not.

Change 1: Universal frontmatter fields. Change 2: User-token chain pattern. Change 3: Per-doc-type state vocabulary. Change 4: doc_type field. Change 5: Execution-phase artifact frontmatter section. (No mention of skill-binding conventions.)
Canonical-helper-home pattern for shared scripts; does not address whether downstream agents bind auditing-shared as a skill or just invoke its scripts via Bash.
skills: [KB-review-disciplines, KB-documentation-criteria] — no auditing-shared binding; uses scripts via Bash if needed.

findings.impact: Two failure modes: (a) brief-honor — ADR-0029 + ADR-0033 require deviations to surface in discoverable artifact locations AND get explicit ratification when they affect cross-feature norms; the convention-note surfacing is necessary but not sufficient. (b) Downstream contagion — Plan-stage tasks will codify the new convention into the validator's whitelist + 4 agent files; later features authoring new audit-touching agents will be uncertain whether the convention applies to them, lacking an ADR to cite.
findings.recommended_resolution: Two paths: (i) Author a new ADR (ADR-0035) capturing the auditing-shared-as-skill-binding convention, with the rationale that load-bearing context (conceptual model of shared utilities) is warranted for agents that materially depend on multiple auditing-shared scripts; OR (ii) fold into ADR-0032 as a sixth change category covering skill-binding conventions (parallel to Change 5's frontmatter additions). Recommended (i) for one-decision-per-ADR cleanliness (ADR-0032 is already at 5 changes per its own framing). The new ADR is authored by design-composer in reconciliation cycle 3.

findings.summary: Blast-radius for shared-document-reviewer modification (doc_type taxonomy extension) is documented at the Change Impact Map level but the actual dependent set across the project is unaccounted for
findings.location: blueprint-v4.md Change Impact Map line 596; Component 6 (lines 897-904); ADR-0032 Change 4 (doc_type field as universal required)
findings.description: shared-document-reviewer is the only modified existing agent in this feature. The Change Impact Map line 596 marks it 'edit (doc_type taxonomy extension per ADR-0032 + D-9 second role)'. ADR-0032 Change 4 elevates `doc_type` to a universal required frontmatter field across all pipeline doc types (~20 doc_type values). Per blast-radius discipline: every existing artifact, template, and agent that authors an artifact has `doc_type` in its blast radius. Manual grep against `.claude/agents/*.md` and `.claude/skills/KB-documentation-criteria/references/templates/*.md` is the appropriate Lens-2 method here (GitNexus would just enumerate the same set). The Blueprint enumerates the touch-points partially — Change Impact Map line 609 covers the templates, but does NOT enumerate the 31 planning-side agents that author artifacts and would need their authoring frontmatter to include `doc_type` (this is the 'doc_type backfill' question). The Migration Strategy section (lines 1924-1931) addresses historical archives ('historical artifacts are not required to add doc_type'), which handles the past. But the present-set — every planning-side agent that authors a new artifact post-ratification — must be modified to emit `doc_type` in its frontmatter. The Blueprint does not enumerate which planning-side agents are affected nor what their modification surface is. Per AC-FR-11-d, the validator's enforcement is scoped to post-implementation date forward, but enforcement on what — agents that don't emit `doc_type` fail the validator at Gate 0 (frontmatter check). The blast-radius is wider than the 1 modified agent the Change Impact Map currently shows.

evidence.quote_paraphrase: shared-document-reviewer.md: edit (doc_type taxonomy extension). KB-documentation-criteria/references/shared-conventions.md: edit (Plan + Execution) — Per ADR-0032 (5 changes); spec-level edits happen at Plan + Execution time.
doc_type field — add as required universal field with 20-value enum covering all pipeline-stage outputs plus 5 execution-phase artifact types.

doc_type field backfill: per AC-FR-11-d's scoping rule, historical artifacts are not required to add doc_type. The validator will tolerate missing doc_type on artifacts whose generated: timestamp predates the feature's deployment date.
Each authors a primary artifact (PRD, Blueprint, Plan, etc.); after this feature ratifies, each must emit doc_type in artifact frontmatter or fail validator at Gate 0.

findings.impact: Blast-radius gap. Plan-stage task generation that follows the Change Impact Map alone will create 1 task to modify shared-document-reviewer + N tasks to update templates, but will NOT generate tasks to update the 31 planning-side agents' authoring prompts to emit `doc_type`. The first post-ratification pipeline run will then trigger validator failures at Gate 0 for every artifact those agents author (because none emit `doc_type`). The migration-scoping rule excuses historical artifacts but does not excuse newly-authored ones.
findings.recommended_resolution: Add to Change Impact Map a row enumerating the planning-side agents (or a wildcard '.claude/agents/intake-*.md, design-*.md, discovery-*.md, finalize-*.md, plan-author.md, test-*.md — author-prompt update to emit `doc_type` per the per-doc-type ADR-0032 enum') with action `edit (small)` and disposition 'minimal prompt amendment to author-time frontmatter section'. Quantify the touch count (likely 20+ agents, ~1-line change each). Alternatively, ship the validator with a grace period (e.g., 'doc_type missing emits warning, not failure, for the first 2 feature runs after ratification') — but this would require AC-FR-11-d revision. Recommend the explicit enumeration approach because it aligns with the Plan-stage task-generation pattern.

findings.summary: FR-7-c floor coverage via Path B is internally defensible but the Blueprint's own internal-consistency narrative leaves ADR-0033 enumerating only 5 artifacts (omitting frontmatter-validation report and execution-reconciliation log per the PRD's 5-item floor)
findings.location: blueprint-v4.md AC-FR-7 floor coverage section (lines 2146-2158); ADR-0033 Context lines 27-31; PRD AC-FR-7-c line 264
findings.description: Path B (resolved as I-AA-001 in audit r1, retained through v2/v3/v4) disposes of the 'frontmatter-validation report' floor item as the script-output schema in `validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py` source, and the 'execution-reconciliation log' floor item as equivalent to `pipeline-run-summary.json`. ADR-0033's Extended Scope-Deviation surfacing table (lines 43-52) covers 8 rows including stub-vs-real audits, discipline-5 mechanical findings, state-transition failures, and run-termination — comprehensive. But the implicit-equivalence of pipeline-run-summary to 'execution-reconciliation log' is left without explicit mapping inside ADR-0033, which means a future reader cross-referencing PRD floor → ADR-0033 enumerated artifacts will see a 5-vs-5 match by count but miss that one of them is the PRD's 'execution-reconciliation log' under a different name. PRD floor item 'frontmatter-validation report' → Blueprint disposition: Covered by JSON-output schema defined inline in validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py source. findings.impact: Path B disposition is sound; the issue is that ADR-0033 (the authoritative cross-feature ADR) doesn't mirror the Blueprint's explicit Path B mapping. A future feature reading ADR-0033 will see 5 execution-phase artifacts and not know that one of them ('pipeline-run-summary') is the PRD's 'execution-reconciliation log' and that the PRD's 'frontmatter-validation report' is intentionally not in the ADR's enumeration (because it lives as a script-output schema, not a pair-pattern artifact). Lower severity than I-AA-604 because the discoverable evidence (Blueprint Path B section) bridges the gap; but the ADR is the cross-feature canonical artifact, so it should hold the mapping too.

— per Blueprint Path B disposition'; (2) 'frontmatter-validation report exists as a JSON-output schema in validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py source rather than a pair-pattern artifact — outside ADR-0033's per-artifact-Scope-Deviation surfacing scope.' findings.summary: 12-state machine + 12 transitions inventory has implicit boundary states (INIT, TERMINATED) that the validator's invariant #10 cycle-count equivalence check needs to handle
findings.description: Line 1413: 'Plus implicit boundary states INIT (orchestrator startup) and TERMINATED (final).' These two boundary states bring the actual state count to 14, not 12. The 12-state title is a documented convention but invariant #10 (cycle counter equivalence: 'at any moment, the orchestrator's in-memory cycle counter MUST equal the count of corresponding T4/T10 entries in state-transitions.log') depends on which transitions are logged. The state diagram (mermaid lines 1434-1456) shows INIT-to-pending and various-to-TERMINATED transitions, but the 12-transition inventory (lines 1417-1430) does NOT enumerate them. The validator's invariant check would need to know whether INIT-to-pending and terminal-to-TERMINATED transitions are logged or skipped; the Blueprint does not specify.

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Plus implicit boundary states INIT (orchestrator startup) and TERMINATED (final).

evidence.section: State Transitions — Transitions (12 total per cc-design.md D-16)
evidence.quote_paraphrase: Table T1-T12. T1 = pending→producing. (No INIT→pending entry; no terminal→TERMINATED entries.)
[*] --> pending: orchestrator initialized. phase_complete --> [*]: gate-pass to Deliverable Packaging. escalated_*_quality --> [*]: user resolution. (Diagram shows INIT and TERMINATED transitions.)
at any moment, the orchestrator's in-memory cycle counter MUST equal the count of corresponding T4/T10 entries in state-transitions.log.

findings.impact: Minor: invariant #10 specifies T4 + T10 only (per-task and phase reconciliation cycles), so the boundary transitions don't directly affect the invariant. But the discrepancy between '12 states / 12 transitions' (table count) and 'INIT + 12 + TERMINATED states / 12 + boundary-entry + boundary-exit transitions' (diagram) is an under-transcription. A Plan author writing the validator would need to decide whether to log INIT→pending and might pick differently from the orchestrator's actual behavior, breaking invariant #10's equivalence.
findings.recommended_resolution: Either (a) document boundary transitions as 'T0 (INIT→pending, fired on orchestrator startup)' and 'T13 (any state → TERMINATED, fired on gate-pass / user-resolution / abort)' to make the inventory match the diagram; OR (b) explicitly state that boundary transitions are NOT logged (and explain how the validator handles the resulting absence). Recommended (a) for completeness — also clarifies invariant #5 'application-level hook fires on EVERY transition'.

verdict_rationale: Per KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md: any BLOCKER → needs_revision (mandatory). I-AA-601 alone forces this verdict — the Frontmatter validator coverage subsection codifies a validator spec that would mechanically reject the very agents v4 declares correct, directly undermining FR-6's mechanical defense. The simulated r5 'pass' verdict is retracted; the simulated audits' scope (verifying v4's surgical corrections were applied) was narrow and missed the broader internal-consistency, brief-honor, and blast-radius concerns this authoritative round 6 surfaced.

Both verdicts can be simultaneously true relative to their scopes: the v3→v4 surgical corrections WERE applied correctly (r5 scope), AND the Blueprint v4 as a whole has 1 BLOCKER + 5 MAJOR issues a full audit surfaces (r6 scope).
